text: Understanding the neural basis of retronasal olfaction is important because the aroma released during the orosensory processing of food has great impact on appetite and satiety [ 20 – 23 ]. Studies have shown that food related odors induce salivation and release insulin and gastric acid [ 24 ]. Many diseases and medications affect the sense of smell, which also alters flavor perception, with the potential to aggravate the patient's health [ 25 , 26 ]. The importance of flavor on metabolic disease related to feeding has been clearly established [ 5 ].
source_label: Direct Behavioral and Neurophysiological Evidence for Retronasal Olfaction in Mice
